title: Founding field run — cost structure and end-to-end incident receipt

run_window.hours_source: arbiter closing summary; carried as an approximation, not a measured value
run_window.calendar_days_note: calendar dates on which some role produced receipts (UTC); coverage differs per role — the executor stream starts 2026-08-17 and all streams end by 2026-08-22 — so these are activity dates, not proof of the run’s precise start/end
run_window.roles: three pluggable model slots (interactive editor agent as arbiter, high-throughput agent runtime as executor, independent reviewer session)

activity_spans.definition: first-to-last receipt timestamp differences per role, computed over strict JSONL-parsed envelope.type==turn.step.completed events within each anchored prefix; these bound each role's recorded activity, not the task's wall-clock start/end
activity_spans.interpretation: role spans differ because sessions start and end at different moments; no single source proves the task's absolute start/end

metric_definitions.native_total: sum of input tokens plus output tokens for completed turns; provider cache-read/cache-write counters are diagnostic subcounters of input and are never added on top of it
metric_definitions.arbiter_source: editor stop-hook completion receipts; each carries input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens
metric_definitions.runtime_role_source: session-API event stream turn.step.completed usage records carrying inputOther, inputCacheRead, output (inputCacheCreation was zero throughout)
metric_definitions.reviewer_window_note: window = the first 1,262 real turn.step.completed events in stream order (envelope.type parsed per JSONL line; substring/grep counting is not used); the 9 appended post-run steps are events 1263–1271 and are excluded and reported separately

shares_pct_of_grand_total.definition: role.native_total / totals.grand_total_native_tokens * 100, rounded to six decimals

budget_target_check.contracted_target: <2% of total tokens for the arbiter (spec section 3.1)
budget_target_check.protocol_significance: the paper-trail honesty gate caught a would-be '<2% achieved' marketing claim before publication; the measured figure is published instead of the target

end_to_end_incident.failure_class: internal probe passes while user path fails (spec section 11, row 7)
end_to_end_incident.observed: service-layer retrieval answered correctly with 8/8 verified catalog heads surfaced, while the real user messaging channel returned nothing for the same questions
end_to_end_incident.admission: the arbiter recorded that acceptance had only exercised the service layer and not the real channel, classified the miss as a P0 incident, and ordered an end-to-end diagnosis
end_to_end_incident.root_cause: query-time full embedding: answering a question embedded all 4421 indexed surfaces first, extrapolating to about 45.6 seconds per query at scale
end_to_end_incident.fix: query-only embedding plus a prestored join, with index maintenance moved into worker cycles and a warmed index

independent_reverification.result: all 8 catalog heads surfaced with complete names
current-state entity parsed and latest-progress slot hit

end_to_end_incident.closure: reviewer confirmed the P0 fix end to end against the real channel; closure ruling recorded in the run ledger (turn 173 review entry)

provenance.algorithm: sha256 over newline-joined canonical JSON (keys sorted, ensure_ascii) of the 68 stop events carrying token counters, ordered by (generation_id, loop_count); replayable off-repository by rerunning the same extraction over the private hook logs

sha256 of exactly the first byte_length bytes of the append-only source; the file may keep growing afterwards, so a longer file with a matching prefix validates this anchor — full-file hashes are deliberately not used for live sources
provenance.cutoff: through the last turn_ended record at extraction time

provenance.algorithm: sha256 of exactly the first byte_length bytes of the append-only source; see the transcript entry for why full-file hashes are not used

cutoff.appended_note: appended lines contained no turn.step.completed events; counted totals are unaffected

provenance.algorithm: sha256 of exactly the first byte_length bytes of the source, parsed as JSONL one event per line; the file is append-only and may keep growing afterwards — a longer file whose matching prefix validates this anchor. Full-file hashes are deliberately not used for live sources.

cutoff.definition: line ending the 1,262nd real turn.step.completed event (envelope.type parsed per JSONL line)
cutoff.appended_note: the appended segment holds the 9 post-run completion events (events 1263–1271) plus later non-counted records; counted totals bind to this prefix only

provenance.algorithm: sha256 of exactly the first byte_length bytes of the append-only source; see the transcript entry for why full-file hashes are not used
provenance.cutoff: through ledger line 1718 — the escalation entry rendered as case-study excerpt C

desensitization_rules_applied: no absolute local paths, conversation or session identifiers, memory identifiers, person names, company names, product names, or internal hostnames/ports appear in this file
model brands are replaced by generic role descriptions; the real user channel is named generically
verbatim ledger excerpts were semantically rewritten in English rather than quoted
source files remain private; these SHA-256 anchors are one-way and reveal no content
open_questions: the task's exact wall-clock start/end: role-level activity spans are receipt-bounded (activity_spans), but no single authorized source proves the absolute start/end behind the ~92-hour approximation
concrete instance receipts for failure classes 1-6 remain class-level public descriptions without published receipts
per-step latency distribution across the whole run is not part of this receipt
